evidence: Actual Chromium runs the production-built tree panel/hook and forwards real GraphQL requests to the owned ASGI/PostgreSQL API and mTLS operator with actual Helm 4. Source/access metadata is supplied by the owned fixture, not a mocked GraphQL result.

The driver discards a successful preparation response. UI review and explicit original-token private retry recover the same prepared tree digest/decimal bytes, with one native tree attempt and no automatic replay.

The browser journal is durable before preparation and binds the exact private input hash. Review/retry send no new private body. Neither raw options/request text nor the bearer token reach browser storage; authentication stays in the private forwarding driver.

The common native fixture preserves original operation/plan/chart rows, native receipt, install guard, run membership and linked reservations. It also covers compiled CLI cold same-endpoint/instance recovery. The binary hash remains unchanged throughout the qualified browser case.
Full TypeScript checking, changed-file ESLint/formatting, 43 targeted story/hook cases and the complete production Storybook build pass.
limitations: Owned Storybook metadata injection and private bearer forwarding do not qualify authenticated Next.js login/routes or automatic access/source discovery.
Native failed receipt/deployment and Kubernetes GETs are controlled fixtures, not retained Linux installation proof. This scenario explicitly configures the supported 300-second agent timeout.

Native template-rendering primitive integration, Kustomize/Helm manifest freezing, image/private registry closure, fresh skipped-resource/credential proof, remaining-only selection and linked execution remain open.
No retained VM restart, original native replay, main merge or production deployment.
